text:
morgan: heads up — saw a customer hit duplicate resource creates when our python async client retries on 5xx while the auth token refresh race happens. not sure if idempotency keys are preserved during the replay.
lee: ugh. repro steps? :eyes:
morgan: quick repro attached below. using async client + `RetryConfig(max_attempts=3, backoff_factor=0.5)` and the token refresh callback that swaps the Authorization header. when the first attempt 502s, we retry, but the server sees no `Idempotency-Key` on the retry and creates a second resource.
lee: can you paste the minimal snippet?
morgan: sure — simplified:
```python
async def create_item(client):
    headers = {"Idempotency-Key": str(uuid4())}
    await client.post("/items", json={"name": "x"}, headers=headers)

# client is AsyncRedwoodClient with an auth hook that does `await refresh_token_if_needed()`
# retry is handled inside client, streams are sent as json body (ok here), but header mutation race looks suspect
```
anita: does the token refresh run in a background task that mutates shared headers? we should avoid mutating a global headers dict across async retries.
sam: i dug into the transport layer — when we start a replay we re-prepare the request, but we were copying headers from the original request object which might have been mutated by the auth hook in-between attempts. so if the auth hook replaces the Authorization header by swapping the headers dict reference, the retry uses the *old* headers object or sometimes ends up missing ephemeral headers like `Idempotency-Key`.
lee: so two issues: (1) header mutation pattern, (2) our retry reconstitution logic doesn't ensure idempotency header survives.
morgan: customer impact: duplicate chargeable resource created. they only saw it under high load + token expiry windows.
anita: quick mitigation — ensure our client treats headers as immutable per-request: deep copy headers at attempt start and re-insert idempotency key if present on first try. also update docs to warn against sharing mutable header objects.
sam: agree. small patch idea: in async_transport.py where we call _prepare_request_for_retry(req) do `req.headers = dict(req.headers)` and if req._original_headers.get("Idempotency-Key") then set it explicitly. i'll open PR.
morgan: thanks. can we also surface a telemetry tag in console that shows when a retry lost idempotency key? that'll help customer debugging.
lee: can add a metric `client.retry.idempotency_missing` with labels model+route.
ci-bot: created issue #2872: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2872 (py-async-retry-idempotency-header-loss) by sam
morgan: putting this on the monday triage agenda for prioritization. cc @sam to own patch. :thumbsup:
sam: will draft fix + unit test. repro case will be added to flaky-replay-suite.
anita: also adding a short note to the auth guide about "avoid mutating header containers across coroutines".
lee: thanks all — good catch. follow up in the issue with a small diff, and let's run customer repro after patch. :rocket:
